reason: The verdict holds: axis-flip TTA STAYS CLOSED on x138. One piece of evidence in the finding is incomplete. VALUE: (1) Probe 19 (exp37, RESULTS.md l.52) = 0.946 vs exp29 0.947, after a 12-video lab gain of +0.0214 (pilkwang) and +0.0187 (a scratch primary that never saw 44b6; l.107). That is the direct failed transfer control for this exact change, and it is stronger evidence than the Z-flip analogy in (b). (2) The finding leaves out probe 25 (exp44 v2 = takaito exp43 + axis-flip + division hygiene) = 0.946 vs probe 24 exp43 = 0.944 on the same day (CONTEXT l.1228-1231). The curator's rule is that our kernels are deterministic, so a 0.001 step is real on the public embryo (l.1909). Hygiene alone scored -0.001 (probe 18). That puts axis-flip at roughly +0.002..+0.003 on the takaito base and -0.001 on exp29. So '(c) the public -0.001 is a real read' is only half the public evidence. The public sign depends on the base, which argues for more variance on private, not for reopening. Expected value on x138 is about +0.0005 centre, range -0.001..+0.003, and it is not predictable. (3) There is also a harm channel specific to x138. x138 still runs the sjlee D4 group (flips + rot90 + transpose) for detection and edge-feature TTA (ext_x138 cell 4) and for DeepCenter (cell 5). The V1284 head is an MLP on z-scored 224-d UNet features captured under that pipeline (CONTEXT l.1382-1395). Swapping the view group shifts its inputs, and it also moves the 0.965 readmit/lowdet pools and the DaughterNet insertion inputs. exp60 is in-sample for pilkwang, which was trained on all 199 clips, so no honest lab exists. (4) The Z-flip probes 12/16 were edge-feature TTA only. As a lab-to-LB control with the same B26 design, point (b) still stands. Just do not call it detection-map evidence (round 2 correction). FEASIBILITY: (a) is correct. Axis-flip replaces views and does not add any (8 = 8), so runtime headroom is irrelevant. The surgery exists (exp37 apply_axis_flip_tta) but would need new anchors for x138's inline rot90 blocks and DeepCenter. It is a node-set changer under R4 (+0.002 needed; never adopt on lab gain). Under f2 it cannot displace the F2 twin. A probe beyond the approved batch needs a new user OK. Spending a slot and a dummy cycle before the 27 Sep 12:00 R8 cutoff costs more than a small, sign-unstable expected gain is worth.
